instructions: This is an infrastructure smoke test, not a scientific benchmark. On the assigned GPU, add the two vectors in data.json with a real CUDA kernel. A standard-library-only helper cuda_add.py is provided; it uses the NVIDIA driver directly and requires no PyTorch installation. Run the helper on the GPU using --input INPUT/data.json --output OUTPUT/result.json. Inspect the helper if needed. Copy result.json back and submit it as /submission/result.json on the current agent machine, then call sie-action test. Report any GPU or transfer failure; do not fabricate a CUDA result.

input.description: Two short vectors to add on the GPU.
CUDA vector-add helper using only Python standard library and the NVIDIA driver.

submission.description: CUDA result with values, backend and GPU name.

environment.name: Python
environment.description: Standard Python; GPU driver is available on the allocated H machine.

requirement: Execute an actual CUDA kernel on the assigned GPU and return its output to the current agent machine.
